rows.question: What does error KST-2044 mean and how do I fix it?

answer.answer: Error KST-2044 occurs when a data source refuses a connection from Kestrel because the database only accepts connections from an allowlist of IP addresses that does not include the Kestrel addresses. To fix this, ask the customer to add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist of their database or firewall.

# Kestrel Analytics — Support Runbook: Error Codes

Internal document · Owner: Customer Support · Last reviewed: 2 September 2026

## How to use this runbook

Every error shown to a Kestrel user carries a code of the form `KST-` followed by four digits. The first digit gives the area: 1 for sign-in, 2 for connectors, 3 for queries and dashboards, 4 for members and seats, 5 for delivery and embedding, 6 for billing.

For each code, this runbook gives what the user sees, the usual cause, what support can do, and when to escalate. Always ask the customer for the workspace name, the exact code and the time it happened. If a code is not listed here, escalate it to the on-call engineer of the Platform team.

Escalations go to the team that owns the service involved. The owning team of each service and its on-call channel are listed in the Service Catalog.

| SEV-1 | Many customers cannot use Kestrel, or data is exposed | 15 minutes, page on-call |
| SEV-2 | One customer is blocked in production, no workaround | 1 hour |
| SEV-3 | Degraded behaviour with a workaround | Next business day |
| SEV-4 | Question, cosmetic issue | Normal

rows.question: What happens, step by step, when a customer's card payment fails?

answer.answer: When a payment fails, the workspace Owner and the billing contact are notified via e-mail immediately. The system then performs automatic retries 1 day, 3 days, and 7 days after the initial attempt. If all retries fail, a 21-day grace period begins, during which the workspace remains fully functional. After this grace period, the workspace enters a read-only mode. If the payment remains unpaid 60 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace is suspended.

## 7. Failed payments

When a payment fails, the workspace Owner and the billing contact receive an e-mail straight away. We then retry the payment automatically 1 day, 3 days and 7 days after the first attempt.

Each retry uses the payment method on file at the time of the retry, so updating the card before the next retry is usually enough to solve the problem. No late fee is charged.

If all retries fail, the workspace enters a grace period of 21 days from the first failed attempt, during which everything keeps working. A banner reminds Admins that payment is overdue.

After the grace period, the workspace becomes read-only: members can view dashboards but cannot edit them, scheduled reports are paused, and datasets stop refreshing.

If the amount is still unpaid 60 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace is suspended: nobody can sign in to it until the outstanding amount is paid. A suspended workspace is not deleted, and returns to normal as soon as the payment succeeds.

## 3. Payment methods

We accept credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express). Business and Enterprise customers can also pay by bank transfer against an invoice, with payment due within 30 days of the invoice date.

The card on file can be updated by the workspace Owner from **Settings → Plan → Payment method**. We do not store full card numbers; they are held by our payment processor.

An invoice is issued for every charge and sent by e-mail to the billing contact of the workspace. Invoices can also be downloaded from **Settings → Plan → Invoices**. The billing contact and the company details printed on invoices (name, address, VAT number) can be changed by the Owner; changes apply to future invoices only. A corrected copy of a past invoice can be requested from support within 90 days of its date.

## 5. Adding and removing seats

Seats can be added at any time. Added seats are charged immediately, pro-rated to the end of the current billing period.

Seats can be removed at any time, but the reduction takes effect at the next renewal. No credit is given for removed seats during the current period.

rows.question: Which plans include single sign-on, and how does an admin set it up?

answer.answer: Single sign-on is available on the Business and Enterprise plans. To set it up, an Admin navigates to Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel.

chunks.text:
5.1 Password and two-factor authentication

Members sign in with their e-mail address and a password, unless the workspace uses single sign-on. We strongly recommend turning on two-factor authentication from **Profile → Security**. Kestrel supports authenticator apps that generate time-based six-digit codes. When you turn it on, Kestrel shows 10 backup codes. Each backup code works once. Store them somewhere safe and separate from your authenticator device.

Admins can make two-factor authentication mandatory for every member from **Settings → Security**. Members who have not set it up are asked to do so at their next sign-in.

### 5.2 Single sign-on

On the Business and Enterprise plans, workspaces can use single sign-on with any SAML 2.0 identity provider. To set it up, an Admin opens **Settings → Security → Single sign-on**, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel. We recommend testing with one Admin account before choosing **Enforce for all members**. When single sign-on is enforced, passwords are disabled and two-factor authentication is handled by your identit

If you no longer have your authenticator device, use one of your backup codes at the second-factor prompt, then set up two-factor authentication again from **Profile → Security**.

rows.question: Can I get a refund on my annual plan 45 days after it renewed?

answer.answer: Yes, under the current policy (effective 1 March 2026), annual plans can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. Since 45 days is within this 60-day window, you are eligible for a pro-rated refund.

Seats can be added at any time. Added seats are charged immediately, pro-rated to the end of the current billing period.

Seats can be removed at any time. On monthly plans the reduction takes effect at the next monthly charge. On annual plans the reduction takes effect at the next renewal, and no credit is given for the current period.

**Monthly plans** are not refundable. When a monthly plan is cancelled, it remains active until the end of the month already paid.

**Annual plans** can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. The refund is pro-rated from the date of the request: you are refunded the unused full months of the annual period. After 60 days, annual plans are not refundable.

Refund requests must be sent by the workspace Owner, either from **Settings → Plan → Request a refund** or by e-mail to billing@kestrel.example. Approved refunds are processed within 14 days and returned to the original payment method.

## How to use this runbook

Every error shown to a Kestrel user carries a code of the form `KST-` followed by four digits. The first digit gives the area: 1 for sign-in, 2 for connectors, 3 for queries and dashboards, 4 for members and seats, 5 for delivery and embedding, 6 for billing.

For each code, this runbook gives what the user sees, the usual cause, what support can do, and when to escalate. Always ask the customer for the workspace name, the exact code and the time it happened. If a code is not listed here, escalate it to the on-call engineer of the Platform team.

|---|---|---|

| SEV-3 | Degraded behaviour with a workaround | Next business day |
| SEV-4 | Question, cosmetic issue | Normal

### KST-1012 — SSO response rejected

**User sees:** "Your identity provider returned an invalid response."
**Cause:** the identity provider certificate has expired or was rotated, or the clock of the identity provider is out of sync.
**Support action:** ask a workspace Admin to upload the new identity provider metadata in **Settings → Security → Single sign-on**.
**Escalate:** to Identity if the metadata is correct and the error persists.

## Connectors (KST-2xxx)

### KST-2040 — Connection timed out

**User sees:** "Kestrel could not reach your data source in time."
**Cause:** the database is down, overloaded, or behind a firewall that silently drops the connection.
**Support action:** ask the customer to confirm the database is reachable from outside their network, on the host and port configured in the connector.
**Escalate:** to Data Integrations if several customers report it for the same source type at the same time.

### KST-2044 — Source refused the connection

**Cause:** the database only accepts connections from an allowlist of IP addresses, and the Kestrel addresses are missing from it.
**Support action:** ask the customer to add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist of their database or firewall. Adding only one of them leads to errors that come and go, because connections can come from either address.
**Escalate:** no.

### KST-2051 — Credentials rejected

**User sees:** "The username or password for this data source is incorrect."
**Cause:** the database password was changed, or the database user was removed.
**Support action:** an Admin must edit the connector and enter the new credentials. Support cannot see stored credentials.
**Escalate:** no.

**User sees:** "This query took too long and was stopped."
**Cause:** a dataset query ran for more than 120 seconds.
**Support action:** suggest adding a filter, pre-aggregating in the source database, or refreshing less often. The time limit is the same on every plan and cannot be raised.

## 1. What Kestrel does

Kestrel Analytics is a dashboard and business intelligence service for teams. You connect your data sources, build datasets on top of them, and turn those datasets into dashboards that refresh automatically. Dashboards can be shared with colleagues, sent as scheduled PDF reports, or embedded in your own web applications.

Everything in Kestrel lives inside a **workspace**. A workspace has members, connectors, datasets and dashboards. Most customers use one workspace per company; larger organisations sometimes create one workspace per department. Members of one workspace cannot see the content of another workspace, even inside the same organisation.

Each workspace is on exactly one plan. The plan sets the number of seats, how often data refreshes, and which administration features are available.
